title: Observational report: rivers, lakes, mountains, deserts and planetary geometry
purpose: Prepare evidence-first training guidance for AI analysis of water resources, drought, flood extent, river morphology, exposed sediment, paleochannels, terrain and later astronomical geometry.
principles: Keep raw satellite pixels unchanged and reproducible.
Separate observation from interpretation, causal hypothesis and speculation.
Do not label a suspected cause as truth without independent hydrological or geological evidence.
Store acquisition date, sensor, platform, spatial resolution, cloud/shadow quality and provenance.
Use display brightness/contrast only for visualization; never overwrite measurement imagery.
Prefer official, legal and public data sources.

research_cases.role: training example with repeated shoreline retreat and advance
river channel, exposed sediment and sandbar analysis
terrain, elevation, rain-shadow and paleohydrology investigation

hypothesis_registry.statement: Changes in channel morphology and sediment accumulation may influence hydraulic connectivity with side channels, tributaries or managed outflows.
Any dredging or channel intervention should be evaluated together with side-channel/outflow connectivity before implementation.
Terrain height, valley geometry, orographic precipitation and rain-shadow effects should be jointly analysed when comparing the Indian and Tibetan sides of the Himalaya.
Ancient-civilization or intentional large-scale landscape-engineering explanations are speculative unless direct archaeological and geological evidence is found.
River, lake, mountain and stellar geometries may be searched for repeated patterns, but candidate patterns must be compared with randomized/null models to avoid false pattern detection.

recommended_pipeline: causal-hypothesis scoring kept separate from visual detection
human review and reproducible report generation

astronomy_extension.goal: Use learned geometric reasoning for Earth observation and later for time-aware 3D analysis of stars, planets and visible sky geometry.
